title: Leaders Who Act as Jupiter
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article builds an extended analogy between Jupiter's role shielding the solar system from debris and the role good leaders play shielding their teams from distraction and external pressure. It contrasts leaders who position themselves at the center of every decision, forcing teams to orbit around them for direction, with those who position themselves at the edge, absorbing criticism and organizational noise so their teams can focus. The piece includes the specific example of leaders choosing to absorb early negative feedback themselves rather than immediately passing along unfiltered criticism to the team.
points: The article compares Jupiter's protective gravitational role to how good leaders should shield their teams.
Leaders who put themselves at the center of every decision create teams dependent on constant direction.
Effective leaders instead position themselves at the edge, absorbing external criticism and pressure.
One concrete example: leaders choosing to absorb early negative feedback rather than passing it along unfiltered.
quotes: Jupiter’s magnetic field is the strongest in the solar system, over 20,000 times stronger than Earth’s.
They view their most important function as liberating team members from outside distractions and threats to their productivity.
Instead, they operate as if they are at the center of their team, with everything revolving around them.
Strong leaders take on the brunt of external criticism and organizational pressures so their teams can focus on the work that matters.
The best leaders don't act like the Sun, operating like they are the center spoke of all team activity. They act like Jupiter.
